genericProblem: A locally owned asynchronous candidate read must distinguish pending, failed, and completed states; a failed remote logout must still clear app-owned local session state, and that invariant needs a directly red-verifiable proof.
searchedSurfaces: both app roots and their app-owned transport cleanup functions
P5 original business requirements G-03, G-05 and G-10
P5 detailed design P-R2 and P-R6
existing frontend architecture gate and its real self-test

counterexamples.reason: The local result selector already distinguishes failed from pending with loading={!result && !problem}.
Its empty candidate collection is guarded by !problem and is not a failed undefined candidate state.
It uses an explicit lifecycle submitting flag rather than an undefined candidate object as a loading proxy.

findings.finding: Eight Select controls in two P5-changed candidate drawers used loading={!candidates}. Their catch paths keep candidates undefined and set problem, so an already-visible failure still presents a permanent loading spinner.
Both production logout paths already use try/finally and call clearLocalSession in finally, but P5 did not carry a direct source assertion and red mutation for the failed-remote-logout invariant.

RefreshSignal has publish sites but no production subscriber. RTK tags are the current write-refresh authority; the dormant publish has no behavioral effect and deleting it is not required to close S1.
The Claude review intentionally did not execute frontend tests; its artifact-only verification must be replaced by a fresh focused run after the S1 remediation.

preventionDispositions.reason: A bounded AST rule covers candidate state that is cleared before a request and whose catch writes problem; bare loading={!candidate} is rejected, and an actual P5 drawer red mutation must fail.
Both app roots must structurally prove that the exact remote logout await is enclosed by a finally containing clearLocalSession; removal is a real red mutation.
There is no subscriber or functional divergence to repair. Removing a dormant legacy signal would expand a focused S1 repair without changing the P5 user outcome.
The evidence is regenerated from a fresh focused frontend run only after all S1 source and prevention-control edits are complete.
